The majority recited "al-Sur" with the sukun on the waw. Qatadah and Zayd ibn 'Ali recited it with a fatha on it, as the plural of sura (form). The exception in His saying ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ is connected (istithna' muttasil, exception of the same category). The excepted ones are Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil. It was said: Ridwan, the bearers of the Throne, and the keepers of Paradise and Hell.

﴿Then it will be blown again﴾. ukhra may be in the place of the nominative as a deputy of the subject (naib al-fa'il, the grammatical substitute for the agent), and it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, meaning: a blast another (nafkhatan ukhra). It may also be in the place of the accusative, and the substitute for the agent in it is:

﴿Then behold, they are standing, looking﴾. Meaning: all the creatures are standing on their feet, looking at what is said to them, or waiting for that.

The majority recited "qiyam" with the nominative, taking it as the predicate, and "yanzuruna" is in the place of the accusative as a circumstantial clause. Zayd ibn 'Ali recited it with the accusative, as a circumstantial element, and the predicate is "yanzuruna." The element that governs the circumstantial is what governs the sudden particle "idha."

al-Kisa'i said: like when you say: "I went out, and behold, Zayd was sitting."

﴿And the earth shone with the light of its Lord﴾. al-Ishraq is illumination. It is said: "the sun shone" when it lit up, and "sharaqat" when it rose. The meaning of "with the light of its Lord" is: with the justice of its Lord, as al-Hasan and others said.

al-Dahhak said: with the judgement of its Lord. The meaning is that the earth lights up and becomes radiant by the justice that Allah established among its people and the truth He decreed concerning them. So justice is light, and injustice is darkness.

It was said: Allah will create a light on the Day of Resurrection, which He will clothe upon the surface of the earth, and it will shine with it, other than the light of the sun and the moon. There is no barrier to taking it in its literal meaning, for Allah, may He be glorified, is the light of the heavens and the earth.

The majority recited "ashraqat" with the active voice. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-Jawza' and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr recited it in the passive voice.

﴿And the Book will be placed﴾. It was said: it is the Preserved Tablet. Qatadah said: meaning the books and scrolls in which are the deeds of the children of Adam, so one takes his book in his right hand and another takes his in his left. Muqatil said likewise. It was said: it is from the placing by the reckoner of the book of reckoning before him, meaning: the Book was placed for the reckoning.

﴿And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought﴾. Meaning: they will be brought to the place of standing, and they will be asked about what their nations answered them with, and the witnesses who will testify against the nations from the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), as in His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation, that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. It was said: the witnesses are those who were martyred in the way of Allah, and they will testify on the Day of Resurrection for whoever defended the religion of Allah. It was said: they are the guardian angels (hafaza), as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾ [Qaf: 21].

﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning: judgement will be passed between the servants with justice and truth, while they are not wronged, meaning they will not have any of their reward diminished, nor will anything be added to the punishment they deserve.

﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, of good and evil. ﴿And He is best aware of what they do﴾ in the world, He has no need of a recorder, a reckoner or a witness. The Book was placed, and the prophets and witnesses were brought, only to complete the proof and cut off excuses.

Then He, may He be glorified, mentioned the detail of what He had stated concerning the full payment of every soul for what it earned, and said: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾, meaning: the disbelievers will be driven to the Fire in groups, that is, in scattered companies, some following others.

Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Akhfash said: zumaran means companies scattered one after another, and from it is the saying of the poet:

And you see the people at its gates, in groups, one group after another, coming to it.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 39, verse 62–73 (part 2 of 2):

Its derivation is from al-zumr (زمر), which means sound, since a group (jama'ah) is never without sound. ﴿Until, when they reach it, its gates are opened.﴾ That is, the gates of the Fire are opened for them to enter. They are seven gates, and the explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Hijr. ﴿And its keepers say to them﴾: khazanah is the plural of khazin (keeper), like sadanah and sadin (guardian). ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves﴾: that is, from among your own selves, ﴿reciting to you the verses of your Lord﴾ which He sent down to them, ﴿and warning you of the meeting of this your day﴾: that is, warning you of the meeting of this day in which you now find yourselves. They say this to them as a rebuke and reproach. They answer with acknowledgment, and they were not able to resort to the argumentation (jadal) that they used to make excuses with in the world, because the matter had become clear and manifest. Therefore they say, ﴿Yes﴾, meaning: the messengers did indeed come to us with the signs of Allah and warned us of what we would encounter. ﴿But the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers﴾, which is ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together"﴾ [Hud: 119].

When they made this acknowledgment, ﴿it is said: "Enter the gates of Hell"﴾ which have been opened for you, to enter them. The accusative of khalidin (abiding) is a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: intending to abide therein forever. ﴿So wretched is the abode of the arrogant﴾. The object of the dispraise is omitted, meaning: wretched is their abode, Hell. The verification of the word mathwa (abode) has already been given in more than one place.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, that he said: "Its keys."

Abu Ya'la, Yusuf al-Qadi in his Sunan, Abu al-Hasan al-Qattan, Ibn al-Sunni, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from 'Uthman ibn 'Affan who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the words of Allah: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, and he said to me: 'O 'Uthman, you have asked me about a matter that no one asked me about before you. The keys of the heavens and the earth are: There is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, and I seek the forgiveness of Allah, who there is no god but He, the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, who gives life and causes death, and He is Living and does not die, in His hand is the good, and He is over all things Powerful.' Then he mentioned the excellence of these words."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Uthman, who said: "He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to him: 'Inform me about the keys of the heavens and the earth,' and he mentioned it..."

al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it from Abu Hurayrah, from 'Uthman.

al-'Uqayli and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted it from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Uthman.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas that "the Quraysh invited the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they would give him wealth so that he would become the richest man in Makkah, and they would marry him to whatever women he wished, and they would follow his lineage. They said to him: 'This is for you, O Muhammad, and you should refrain from reviling our gods and not mention them with evil.' He said: 'Until I see what comes to me from my Lord.' Then the revelation came: ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾ to the end of the surah, and Allah sent down to him: ﴿Say: Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?﴾ to His words: ﴿among the losers﴾."

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud who said: "A rabbi (habr) of the rabbis came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Muhammad, we find that Allah will carry the heavens on the Day of Resurrection on one finger, the trees on one finger, the water and the moist earth on one finger, and the rest of creation on one finger, and then He says: I am the King.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed, affirming the rabbi's words. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾."

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others transmitted from the narration of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah will seize the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold the heaven with His right hand, then He will say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?"

On this subject there are hadiths and reports that require taking the verse according to its apparent meaning, without straining for interpretation or forcing the sayings of one or another.

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others transmitted from Abu Hurayrah who said: "A man from the Jews in the market of Madinah said: 'By the One who chose Musa over mankind.' A man from the Ansar raised his hand and slapped him, saying: 'Do you say this while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among us?' I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'Allah said: ﴿And the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth swoons, except whom Allah wills. Then it is blown again, and behold, they are standing, looking on﴾. So I will be the first to raise his head, and behold, Musa will be holding onto one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether he raised his head before me, or whether he was among those whom Allah excepted.'"

Abu Ya'la, al-Daraqutni in al-Afrad, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th transmitted from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾, that he said: "They are the martyrs, wearing their swords around His Throne, and the angels will meet them on the Day of Resurrection..." the hadith.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and 'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted it as a saying of Abu Hurayrah.

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in al-Ibanah, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Anas that "he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about His words ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾, and he said: 'Jibril, Mika'il, the Angel of Death, Israfil, and the bearers of the Throne.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Jabir regarding His words ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ that he said: "Musa, because he had been stricken before." The hadiths narrated concerning the manner of the blowing of the Horn are numerous.

'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿And the prophets and the witnesses are brought﴾ that he said: "The prophets are the messengers, and the witnesses are those who bear witness for them that they conveyed the message, [being] not slanderers nor cursers."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him regarding the verse that he said: "They bear witness to the conveying of the message and to the peoples' denial of them."

The point of the refutation is what the fronting (of the object) indicates of restriction (qasr, limiting the action to one object).

Al-Zajjaj said: the word "the name of Allah" is in the accusative governed by u'bud (worship). He said: there is no disagreement about this between the Basran and Kufan grammarians.

Al-Farra' said: it is in the accusative governed by an implied verb, and the like of this was narrated from al-Kisa'i. The first view is more preferable. Al-Zajjaj said: the fa' in fa'bud is for the conditional (al-mujazah, the sense of a condition and its consequence). Al-Akhfash said: it is superfluous (za'ida). 'Ata' and Muqatil said: the meaning of fa'bud is: affirm the Oneness (of Allah), because worship of Him is not valid except with His Oneness.

﴿And be among the grateful﴾, for His favour upon you by guiding you to the Oneness, calling to His religion, and singling you out with the messengership.

﴿And they did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾. Al-Mubarrad said: meaning, they did not magnify Him with His true magnificence, from your saying: "So-and-so is great in measure." He described them with this only because they worshipped other than Allah and commanded His Messenger to be like them in polytheism.

al-Hasan, Abu Haywa and 'Isa ibn 'Umar recited "qaddaru" with the doubling of the dal.

﴿And the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The qabda (handful) in the language is what you grasp with the whole of your palm. He, may He be glorified, informed of the greatness of His power, that the whole earth, with its greatness and density, is within His capacity like a thing which the grasper holds in his hand. As they say: "It is in the hand of so-and-so and in his grasp," for a thing that is easy for him to dispose of, even if he does not actually grasp it. Likewise His saying: ﴿And the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾. The mention of the right hand is for emphasis on the completeness of power, just as one of us folds a thing that is subject to his power, folding it with his right hand. The right hand in the speech of the Arabs may mean power and dominion.

Al-Akhfash said: "in His right hand" means "in His power," like His saying: ﴿or what your right hands possess﴾ [al-Nisa': 3], meaning: what you had power over. Dominion is not for the right hand to the exclusion of the left and the rest of the body. From the same usage is His saying, may He be glorified: ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45], meaning: by strength and power. From the same usage is the saying of the poet:

When a banner is raised for glory, 'Arabah receives it with the right hand.

And the saying of another:

And when I saw the sun, its light shining, I took my need from it with my right hand.

And the saying of another:

It sneezed with a lofty nose, and my hands reached the Pleiades while I was seated, not standing.

The clause ﴿and the earth entirely is His handful﴾ is in the place of the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal): meaning, they did not magnify Him with His true magnification, while the state is that He is described with this attribute which indicates the completeness of power.

The majority recited qabdatuhu with the nominative, taking it as the predicate of the subject. al-Hasan recited it with the accusative, and Ibn Khalawayh explained this as adverbial (zarfiyya), meaning: "within His grasp."

The majority recited "matwiyyat" with the nominative, taking it as the predicate of the subject, and the clause is in the place of the accusative as a circumstantial clause like the one before it. "Bi-yaminihi" is connected to "matwiyyat," or is a circumstantial element from the pronoun in "matwiyyat," or is a second predicate. 'Isa and al-Jahdari recited "matwiyyatin" with the accusative. The reasoning for this is that "the heavens" is conjoined to "the earth," and "qabdatuhu" is the predicate about the earth and the heavens, and "matwiyyat" is a circumstantial element, or "matwiyyatin" is in the accusative governed by an implied verb, and "bi-yaminihi" is the predicate.

The Day of Resurrection was singled out for mention, although His power is all-encompassing, because claims will be cut off on it, as He, may He be glorified, said: ﴿The dominion that Day belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Hajj: 56], and He said: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgement﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4]. Then He, may He be glorified, declared Himself far removed: ﴿Glory be to Him and exalted above what they associate with Him﴾, meaning from the objects of worship which they make partners to Him, together with this great power and dazzling wisdom.

﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon﴾. This is the first blast. The sur (horn) is the trumpet into which Israfil blows, and this has been discussed more than once before. The meaning of "swoon" (sa'iqa) is that their minds are taken away and they fall unconscious. It was said: they die.

al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said: the people of the heavens and the earth die from terror and the intensity of the sound.

The majority recited "al-Sur" with the sukun on the waw. Qatadah and Zayd ibn 'Ali recited it with a fatha on it, as the plural of sura (form). The exception in His saying ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ is connected (istithna' muttasil, exception of the same category). The excepted ones are Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil. It was said: Ridwan, the bearers of the Throne, and the keepers of Paradise and Hell.

﴿Then it will be blown again﴾. ukhra may be in the place of the nominative as a deputy of the subject (naib al-fa'il, the grammatical substitute for the agent), and it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, meaning: a blast another (nafkhatan ukhra). It may also be in the place of the accusative, and the substitute for the agent in it is:

﴿Then behold, they are standing, looking﴾. Meaning: all the creatures are standing on their feet, looking at what is said to them, or waiting for that.

The majority recited "qiyam" with the nominative, taking it as the predicate, and "yanzuruna" is in the place of the accusative as a circumstantial clause. Zayd ibn 'Ali recited it with the accusative, as a circumstantial element, and the predicate is "yanzuruna." The element that governs the circumstantial is what governs the sudden particle "idha."

al-Kisa'i said: like when you say: "I went out, and behold, Zayd was sitting."

﴿And the earth shone with the light of its Lord﴾. al-Ishraq is illumination. It is said: "the sun shone" when it lit up, and "sharaqat" when it rose. The meaning of "with the light of its Lord" is: with the justice of its Lord, as al-Hasan and others said.

al-Dahhak said: with the judgement of its Lord. The meaning is that the earth lights up and becomes radiant by the justice that Allah established among its people and the truth He decreed concerning them. So justice is light, and injustice is darkness.

It was said: Allah will create a light on the Day of Resurrection, which He will clothe upon the surface of the earth, and it will shine with it, other than the light of the sun and the moon. There is no barrier to taking it in its literal meaning, for Allah, may He be glorified, is the light of the heavens and the earth.

The majority recited "ashraqat" with the active voice. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-Jawza' and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr recited it in the passive voice.

﴿And the Book will be placed﴾. It was said: it is the Preserved Tablet. Qatadah said: meaning the books and scrolls in which are the deeds of the children of Adam, so one takes his book in his right hand and another takes his in his left. Muqatil said likewise. It was said: it is from the placing by the reckoner of the book of reckoning before him, meaning: the Book was placed for the reckoning.

﴿And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought﴾. Meaning: they will be brought to the place of standing, and they will be asked about what their nations answered them with, and the witnesses who will testify against the nations from the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), as in His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation, that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. It was said: the witnesses are those who were martyred in the way of Allah, and they will testify on the Day of Resurrection for whoever defended the religion of Allah. It was said: they are the guardian angels (hafaza), as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾ [Qaf: 21].

﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning: judgement will be passed between the servants with justice and truth, while they are not wronged, meaning they will not have any of their reward diminished, nor will anything be added to the punishment they deserve.

﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, of good and evil. ﴿And He is best aware of what they do﴾ in the world, He has no need of a recorder, a reckoner or a witness. The Book was placed, and the prophets and witnesses were brought, only to complete the proof and cut off excuses.

Then He, may He be glorified, mentioned the detail of what He had stated concerning the full payment of every soul for what it earned, and said: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾, meaning: the disbelievers will be driven to the Fire in groups, that is, in scattered companies, some following others.

Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Akhfash said: zumaran means companies scattered one after another, and from it is the saying of the poet:

And you see the people at its gates, in groups, one group after another, coming to it.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 39, verse 62–73 (part 2 of 2):

Its derivation is from al-zumr (زمر), which means sound, since a group (jama'ah) is never without sound. ﴿Until, when they reach it, its gates are opened.﴾ That is, the gates of the Fire are opened for them to enter. They are seven gates, and the explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Hijr. ﴿And its keepers say to them﴾: khazanah is the plural of khazin (keeper), like sadanah and sadin (guardian). ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves﴾: that is, from among your own selves, ﴿reciting to you the verses of your Lord﴾ which He sent down to them, ﴿and warning you of the meeting of this your day﴾: that is, warning you of the meeting of this day in which you now find yourselves. They say this to them as a rebuke and reproach. They answer with acknowledgment, and they were not able to resort to the argumentation (jadal) that they used to make excuses with in the world, because the matter had become clear and manifest. Therefore they say, ﴿Yes﴾, meaning: the messengers did indeed come to us with the signs of Allah and warned us of what we would encounter. ﴿But the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers﴾, which is ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together"﴾ [Hud: 119].

When they made this acknowledgment, ﴿it is said: "Enter the gates of Hell"﴾ which have been opened for you, to enter them. The accusative of khalidin (abiding) is a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: intending to abide therein forever. ﴿So wretched is the abode of the arrogant﴾. The object of the dispraise is omitted, meaning: wretched is their abode, Hell. The verification of the word mathwa (abode) has already been given in more than one place.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, that he said: "Its keys."

Abu Ya'la, Yusuf al-Qadi in his Sunan, Abu al-Hasan al-Qattan, Ibn al-Sunni, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from 'Uthman ibn 'Affan who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the words of Allah: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, and he said to me: 'O 'Uthman, you have asked me about a matter that no one asked me about before you. The keys of the heavens and the earth are: There is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, and I seek the forgiveness of Allah, who there is no god but He, the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, who gives life and causes death, and He is Living and does not die, in His hand is the good, and He is over all things Powerful.' Then he mentioned the excellence of these words."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Uthman, who said: "He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to him: 'Inform me about the keys of the heavens and the earth,' and he mentioned it..."

al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it from Abu Hurayrah, from 'Uthman.

al-'Uqayli and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted it from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Uthman.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas that "the Quraysh invited the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they would give him wealth so that he would become the richest man in Makkah, and they would marry him to whatever women he wished, and they would follow his lineage. They said to him: 'This is for you, O Muhammad, and you should refrain from reviling our gods and not mention them with evil.' He said: 'Until I see what comes to me from my Lord.' Then the revelation came: ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾ to the end of the surah, and Allah sent down to him: ﴿Say: Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?﴾ to His words: ﴿among the losers﴾."

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud who said: "A rabbi (habr) of the rabbis came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Muhammad, we find that Allah will carry the heavens on the Day of Resurrection on one finger, the trees on one finger, the water and the moist earth on one finger, and the rest of creation on one finger, and then He says: I am the King.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed, affirming the rabbi's words. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾."

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others transmitted from the narration of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah will seize the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold the heaven with His right hand, then He will say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?"

On this subject there are hadiths and reports that require taking the verse according to its apparent meaning, without straining for interpretation or forcing the sayings of one or another.

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others transmitted from Abu Hurayrah who said: "A man from the Jews in the market of Madinah said: 'By the One who chose Musa over mankind.' A man from the Ansar raised his hand and slapped him, saying: 'Do you say this while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among us?' I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'Allah said: ﴿And the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth swoons, except whom Allah wills. Then it is blown again, and behold, they are standing, looking on﴾. So I will be the first to raise his head, and behold, Musa will be holding onto one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether he raised his head before me, or whether he was among those whom Allah excepted.'"

Abu Ya'la, al-Daraqutni in al-Afrad, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th transmitted from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾, that he said: "They are the martyrs, wearing their swords around His Throne, and the angels will meet them on the Day of Resurrection..." the hadith.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and 'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted it as a saying of Abu Hurayrah.

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in al-Ibanah, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Anas that "he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about His words ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾, and he said: 'Jibril, Mika'il, the Angel of Death, Israfil, and the bearers of the Throne.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Jabir regarding His words ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ that he said: "Musa, because he had been stricken before." The hadiths narrated concerning the manner of the blowing of the Horn are numerous.

'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿And the prophets and the witnesses are brought﴾ that he said: "The prophets are the messengers, and the witnesses are those who bear witness for them that they conveyed the message, [being] not slanderers nor cursers."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him regarding the verse that he said: "They bear witness to the conveying of the message and to the peoples' denial of them."

﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾, of the things that exist in this world and the Hereafter, whatever they may be, without any distinction between one thing and another. The tafsir of this verse has already been discussed in (Surat) al-An'am. ﴿And He is the Guardian over all things﴾, meaning that all things are entrusted to Him. He is the One who sustains and manages them, with no partner.

﴿To Him belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth﴾. The word maqalid is plural; its singular is miqlid or miqlad, or it has no singular from its own root, like asatir (tales). It means the keys of the heavens and the earth, of provision and of mercy. This was said by Muqatil, Qatadah and others. Al-Layth said: al-miqlad is the treasury. The meaning of the verse is: to Him belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. This was also the view of al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. It was said: the treasuries of the heavens are the rain, and the treasuries of the earth are the plants. It was also said: it is an expression for His power and His preservation of them. The first view is more preferable. Al-Jawhari said: al-iqlid is the key, and then he said: its plural is al-maqalid. It was said: the maqalid are "There is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I seek the forgiveness of Allah, and there is no power nor strength except with Allah." Other views have also been stated.

﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, those are the losers﴾, meaning in the Qur'an and the other signs that point to Allah, may He be glorified, and to His Oneness. The meaning of "the losers" is those who are complete in loss, because by this disbelief they have come to the Fire.

﴿Say: Do you then order me to worship other than Allah, O ignorant ones?﴾ The interrogative here is for reproachful denial (istifham li'l-inkar al-tawbikhi, a question used to rebuke and deny). The fa' is for conjunction with an implied element, as in its counterparts. Ghayra is not in the accusative governed by a'budu. A'budu is governed by tamurunni, on the assumption of the verbal particle an (an al-masdariyya, the particle that turns the following verb into a verbal noun). When it is deleted, its governing power is nullified. The original form is: "Do you then order me that I worship other than Allah?" This was said by al-Kisa'i and others.

It is permissible that ghayra be in the accusative governed by tamurunni, with a'budu being a badal (substitute) for it, a badal al-ishtimal (inclusive apposition, where the substitute is related to the original but not identical to it), and an being implied with it as well.

It is also permissible that ghayra be in the accusative governed by an implied verb, meaning: "Do you then compel me to other than Allah," that is, to the worship of other than Allah; or: "I worship other than Allah"?

He, may He be glorified, commanded him to say this to the disbelievers when they invited him to what they were upon of worshipping idols, and they said: "It is the religion of your fathers."

The majority of readers recited tamurunni with the assimilation of the nun of rafʿ (the nun that marks the nominative/indicative in the verb) into the nun of protection (nun al-wiqaya, the nun that protects the verb's final consonant before the first person pronoun), with differences among them regarding the vowelling and the sukun of the ya'.

Nafi' recited "tamurunniya" with a light nun and a fatha on the ya'. Ibn 'Amir recited "tamurunnani" with the nun separated (al-fakk, not assimilated) and the ya' with sukun.

﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you﴾, meaning from among the messengers: ﴿If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will certainly be among the losers﴾. This statement is by way of allusion (ta'rid) addressed to others than the messengers, because Allah, may He be glorified, has protected them from association. The purpose of stating it in this way is to warn and admonish the servants against associating others with Allah. For if it causes the deeds of the prophets to be nullified, on the supposition and assumption, then it nullifies the deeds of others from their nations all the more so.

It was said: in the speech there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and the meaning is: "It has certainly been revealed to you: If you associate, and it has been revealed to those before you likewise."

Muqatil said: meaning, it was revealed to you and to the prophets before you with the Oneness (of Allah), and the Oneness is omitted. Then he said: "If you associate, O Muhammad, your deeds will be nullified." This address is specifically to the Prophet (ﷺ).

It was said: the singular address in "If you associate" is in consideration of each one of the prophets, as if it were said: it was revealed to you and to each one of the prophets this statement, which is "If you associate." This verse is restricted to dying upon association, as in the other verse: ﴿And whoever of you turns back from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever, those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217]. It was said: this is specific to the prophets, because association from them is a greater sin than association from others. The first view is more preferable.

﴿And the earth shone with the light of its Lord﴾. al-Ishraq is illumination. It is said: "the sun shone" when it lit up, and "sharaqat" when it rose. The meaning of "with the light of its Lord" is: with the justice of its Lord, as al-Hasan and others said.

al-Dahhak said: with the judgement of its Lord. The meaning is that the earth lights up and becomes radiant by the justice that Allah established among its people and the truth He decreed concerning them. So justice is light, and injustice is darkness.

It was said: Allah will create a light on the Day of Resurrection, which He will clothe upon the surface of the earth, and it will shine with it, other than the light of the sun and the moon. There is no barrier to taking it in its literal meaning, for Allah, may He be glorified, is the light of the heavens and the earth.

The majority recited "ashraqat" with the active voice. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-Jawza' and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr recited it in the passive voice.

﴿And the Book will be placed﴾. It was said: it is the Preserved Tablet. Qatadah said: meaning the books and scrolls in which are the deeds of the children of Adam, so one takes his book in his right hand and another takes his in his left. Muqatil said likewise. It was said: it is from the placing by the reckoner of the book of reckoning before him, meaning: the Book was placed for the reckoning.

﴿And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought﴾. Meaning: they will be brought to the place of standing, and they will be asked about what their nations answered them with, and the witnesses who will testify against the nations from the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), as in His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation, that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. It was said: the witnesses are those who were martyred in the way of Allah, and they will testify on the Day of Resurrection for whoever defended the religion of Allah. It was said: they are the guardian angels (hafaza), as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾ [Qaf: 21].

﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning: judgement will be passed between the servants with justice and truth, while they are not wronged, meaning they will not have any of their reward diminished, nor will anything be added to the punishment they deserve.

﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, of good and evil. ﴿And He is best aware of what they do﴾ in the world, He has no need of a recorder, a reckoner or a witness. The Book was placed, and the prophets and witnesses were brought, only to complete the proof and cut off excuses.

Then He, may He be glorified, mentioned the detail of what He had stated concerning the full payment of every soul for what it earned, and said: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾, meaning: the disbelievers will be driven to the Fire in groups, that is, in scattered companies, some following others.

Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Akhfash said: zumaran means companies scattered one after another, and from it is the saying of the poet:

And you see the people at its gates, in groups, one group after another, coming to it.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 39, verse 62–73 (part 2 of 2):

Its derivation is from al-zumr (زمر), which means sound, since a group (jama'ah) is never without sound. ﴿Until, when they reach it, its gates are opened.﴾ That is, the gates of the Fire are opened for them to enter. They are seven gates, and the explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Hijr. ﴿And its keepers say to them﴾: khazanah is the plural of khazin (keeper), like sadanah and sadin (guardian). ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves﴾: that is, from among your own selves, ﴿reciting to you the verses of your Lord﴾ which He sent down to them, ﴿and warning you of the meeting of this your day﴾: that is, warning you of the meeting of this day in which you now find yourselves. They say this to them as a rebuke and reproach. They answer with acknowledgment, and they were not able to resort to the argumentation (jadal) that they used to make excuses with in the world, because the matter had become clear and manifest. Therefore they say, ﴿Yes﴾, meaning: the messengers did indeed come to us with the signs of Allah and warned us of what we would encounter. ﴿But the word of punishment has come due upon the disbelievers﴾, which is ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together"﴾ [Hud: 119].

When they made this acknowledgment, ﴿it is said: "Enter the gates of Hell"﴾ which have been opened for you, to enter them. The accusative of khalidin (abiding) is a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: intending to abide therein forever. ﴿So wretched is the abode of the arrogant﴾. The object of the dispraise is omitted, meaning: wretched is their abode, Hell. The verification of the word mathwa (abode) has already been given in more than one place.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, that he said: "Its keys."

Abu Ya'la, Yusuf al-Qadi in his Sunan, Abu al-Hasan al-Qattan, Ibn al-Sunni, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from 'Uthman ibn 'Affan who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the words of Allah: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾, and he said to me: 'O 'Uthman, you have asked me about a matter that no one asked me about before you. The keys of the heavens and the earth are: There is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, and I seek the forgiveness of Allah, who there is no god but He, the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, who gives life and causes death, and He is Living and does not die, in His hand is the good, and He is over all things Powerful.' Then he mentioned the excellence of these words."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Uthman, who said: "He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to him: 'Inform me about the keys of the heavens and the earth,' and he mentioned it..."

al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it from Abu Hurayrah, from 'Uthman.

al-'Uqayli and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat transmitted it from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Uthman.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas that "the Quraysh invited the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that they would give him wealth so that he would become the richest man in Makkah, and they would marry him to whatever women he wished, and they would follow his lineage. They said to him: 'This is for you, O Muhammad, and you should refrain from reviling our gods and not mention them with evil.' He said: 'Until I see what comes to me from my Lord.' Then the revelation came: ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾ to the end of the surah, and Allah sent down to him: ﴿Say: Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?﴾ to His words: ﴿among the losers﴾."

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud who said: "A rabbi (habr) of the rabbis came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Muhammad, we find that Allah will carry the heavens on the Day of Resurrection on one finger, the trees on one finger, the water and the moist earth on one finger, and the rest of creation on one finger, and then He says: I am the King.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed, affirming the rabbi's words. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾."

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others transmitted from the narration of Abu Hurayrah: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah will seize the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold the heaven with His right hand, then He will say: I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?"

On this subject there are hadiths and reports that require taking the verse according to its apparent meaning, without straining for interpretation or forcing the sayings of one or another.

al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others transmitted from Abu Hurayrah who said: "A man from the Jews in the market of Madinah said: 'By the One who chose Musa over mankind.' A man from the Ansar raised his hand and slapped him, saying: 'Do you say this while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among us?' I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'Allah said: ﴿And the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth swoons, except whom Allah wills. Then it is blown again, and behold, they are standing, looking on﴾. So I will be the first to raise his head, and behold, Musa will be holding onto one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether he raised his head before me, or whether he was among those whom Allah excepted.'"

Abu Ya'la, al-Daraqutni in al-Afrad, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th transmitted from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾, that he said: "They are the martyrs, wearing their swords around His Throne, and the angels will meet them on the Day of Resurrection..." the hadith.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and 'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted it as a saying of Abu Hurayrah.

al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir, Abu Nasr al-Sijzi in al-Ibanah, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Anas that "he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about His words ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾, and he said: 'Jibril, Mika'il, the Angel of Death, Israfil, and the bearers of the Throne.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Jabir regarding His words ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ that he said: "Musa, because he had been stricken before." The hadiths narrated concerning the manner of the blowing of the Horn are numerous.

'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿And the prophets and the witnesses are brought﴾ that he said: "The prophets are the messengers, and the witnesses are those who bear witness for them that they conveyed the message, [being] not slanderers nor cursers."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him regarding the verse that he said: "They bear witness to the conveying of the message and to the peoples' denial of them."

﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾, of the things that exist in this world and the Hereafter, whatever they may be, without any distinction between one thing and another. The tafsir of this verse has already been discussed in (Surat) al-An'am. ﴿And He is the Guardian over all things﴾, meaning that all things are entrusted to Him. He is the One who sustains and manages them, with no partner.

﴿To Him belong the keys (maqalid) of the heavens and the earth﴾. The word maqalid is plural; its singular is miqlid or miqlad, or it has no singular from its own root, like asatir (tales). It means the keys of the heavens and the earth, of provision and of mercy. This was said by Muqatil, Qatadah and others. Al-Layth said: al-miqlad is the treasury. The meaning of the verse is: to Him belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. This was also the view of al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. It was said: the treasuries of the heavens are the rain, and the treasuries of the earth are the plants. It was also said: it is an expression for His power and His preservation of them. The first view is more preferable. Al-Jawhari said: al-iqlid is the key, and then he said: its plural is al-maqalid. It was said: the maqalid are "There is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, I seek the forgiveness of Allah, and there is no power nor strength except with Allah." Other views have also been stated.

﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, those are the losers﴾, meaning in the Qur'an and the other signs that point to Allah, may He be glorified, and to His Oneness. The meaning of "the losers" is those who are complete in loss, because by this disbelief they have come to the Fire.

﴿Say: Do you then order me to worship other than Allah, O ignorant ones?﴾ The interrogative here is for reproachful denial (istifham li'l-inkar al-tawbikhi, a question used to rebuke and deny). The fa' is for conjunction with an implied element, as in its counterparts. Ghayra is not in the accusative governed by a'budu. A'budu is governed by tamurunni, on the assumption of the verbal particle an (an al-masdariyya, the particle that turns the following verb into a verbal noun). When it is deleted, its governing power is nullified. The original form is: "Do you then order me that I worship other than Allah?" This was said by al-Kisa'i and others.

It is permissible that ghayra be in the accusative governed by tamurunni, with a'budu being a badal (substitute) for it, a badal al-ishtimal (inclusive apposition, where the substitute is related to the original but not identical to it), and an being implied with it as well.

It is also permissible that ghayra be in the accusative governed by an implied verb, meaning: "Do you then compel me to other than Allah," that is, to the worship of other than Allah; or: "I worship other than Allah"?

He, may He be glorified, commanded him to say this to the disbelievers when they invited him to what they were upon of worshipping idols, and they said: "It is the religion of your fathers."

The majority of readers recited tamurunni with the assimilation of the nun of rafʿ (the nun that marks the nominative/indicative in the verb) into the nun of protection (nun al-wiqaya, the nun that protects the verb's final consonant before the first person pronoun), with differences among them regarding the vowelling and the sukun of the ya'.

Nafi' recited "tamurunniya" with a light nun and a fatha on the ya'. Ibn 'Amir recited "tamurunnani" with the nun separated (al-fakk, not assimilated) and the ya' with sukun.

﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you﴾, meaning from among the messengers: ﴿If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified, and you will certainly be among the losers﴾. This statement is by way of allusion (ta'rid) addressed to others than the messengers, because Allah, may He be glorified, has protected them from association. The purpose of stating it in this way is to warn and admonish the servants against associating others with Allah. For if it causes the deeds of the prophets to be nullified, on the supposition and assumption, then it nullifies the deeds of others from their nations all the more so.

It was said: in the speech there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and the meaning is: "It has certainly been revealed to you: If you associate, and it has been revealed to those before you likewise."

Muqatil said: meaning, it was revealed to you and to the prophets before you with the Oneness (of Allah), and the Oneness is omitted. Then he said: "If you associate, O Muhammad, your deeds will be nullified." This address is specifically to the Prophet (ﷺ).

It was said: the singular address in "If you associate" is in consideration of each one of the prophets, as if it were said: it was revealed to you and to each one of the prophets this statement, which is "If you associate." This verse is restricted to dying upon association, as in the other verse: ﴿And whoever of you turns back from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever, those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217]. It was said: this is specific to the prophets, because association from them is a greater sin than association from others. The first view is more preferable.

Then Allah, may He be glorified, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to affirm His Oneness, saying: ﴿Rather, worship Allah alone﴾. In this there is a refutation of the polytheists, since they commanded him to worship idols. The point of the refutation is what the fronting (of the object) indicates of restriction (qasr, limiting the action to one object).

Al-Zajjaj said: the word "the name of Allah" is in the accusative governed by u'bud (worship). He said: there is no disagreement about this between the Basran and Kufan grammarians.

Al-Farra' said: it is in the accusative governed by an implied verb, and the like of this was narrated from al-Kisa'i. The first view is more preferable. Al-Zajjaj said: the fa' in fa'bud is for the conditional (al-mujazah, the sense of a condition and its consequence). Al-Akhfash said: it is superfluous (za'ida). 'Ata' and Muqatil said: the meaning of fa'bud is: affirm the Oneness (of Allah), because worship of Him is not valid except with His Oneness.

﴿And be among the grateful﴾, for His favour upon you by guiding you to the Oneness, calling to His religion, and singling you out with the messengership.

﴿And they did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾. Al-Mubarrad said: meaning, they did not magnify Him with His true magnificence, from your saying: "So-and-so is great in measure." He described them with this only because they worshipped other than Allah and commanded His Messenger to be like them in polytheism.

al-Hasan, Abu Haywa and 'Isa ibn 'Umar recited "qaddaru" with the doubling of the dal.

﴿And the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The qabda (handful) in the language is what you grasp with the whole of your palm. He, may He be glorified, informed of the greatness of His power, that the whole earth, with its greatness and density, is within His capacity like a thing which the grasper holds in his hand. As they say: "It is in the hand of so-and-so and in his grasp," for a thing that is easy for him to dispose of, even if he does not actually grasp it. Likewise His saying: ﴿And the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾. The mention of the right hand is for emphasis on the completeness of power, just as one of us folds a thing that is subject to his power, folding it with his right hand. The right hand in the speech of the Arabs may mean power and dominion.

Al-Akhfash said: "in His right hand" means "in His power," like His saying: ﴿or what your right hands possess﴾ [al-Nisa': 3], meaning: what you had power over. Dominion is not for the right hand to the exclusion of the left and the rest of the body. From the same usage is His saying, may He be glorified: ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 45], meaning: by strength and power. From the same usage is the saying of the poet:

When a banner is raised for glory, 'Arabah receives it with the right hand.

And the saying of another:

And when I saw the sun, its light shining, I took my need from it with my right hand.

And the saying of another:

It sneezed with a lofty nose, and my hands reached the Pleiades while I was seated, not standing.

The clause ﴿and the earth entirely is His handful﴾ is in the place of the accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal): meaning, they did not magnify Him with His true magnification, while the state is that He is described with this attribute which indicates the completeness of power.

The majority recited qabdatuhu with the nominative, taking it as the predicate of the subject. al-Hasan recited it with the accusative, and Ibn Khalawayh explained this as adverbial (zarfiyya), meaning: "within His grasp."

The majority recited "matwiyyat" with the nominative, taking it as the predicate of the subject, and the clause is in the place of the accusative as a circumstantial clause like the one before it. "Bi-yaminihi" is connected to "matwiyyat," or is a circumstantial element from the pronoun in "matwiyyat," or is a second predicate. 'Isa and al-Jahdari recited "matwiyyatin" with the accusative. The reasoning for this is that "the heavens" is conjoined to "the earth," and "qabdatuhu" is the predicate about the earth and the heavens, and "matwiyyat" is a circumstantial element, or "matwiyyatin" is in the accusative governed by an implied verb, and "bi-yaminihi" is the predicate.

The Day of Resurrection was singled out for mention, although His power is all-encompassing, because claims will be cut off on it, as He, may He be glorified, said: ﴿The dominion that Day belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Hajj: 56], and He said: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgement﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4]. Then He, may He be glorified, declared Himself far removed: ﴿Glory be to Him and exalted above what they associate with Him﴾, meaning from the objects of worship which they make partners to Him, together with this great power and dazzling wisdom.

﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon﴾. This is the first blast. The sur (horn) is the trumpet into which Israfil blows, and this has been discussed more than once before. The meaning of "swoon" (sa'iqa) is that their minds are taken away and they fall unconscious. It was said: they die.

al-Wahidi said: the exegetes said: the people of the heavens and the earth die from terror and the intensity of the sound.

The majority recited "al-Sur" with the sukun on the waw. Qatadah and Zayd ibn 'Ali recited it with a fatha on it, as the plural of sura (form). The exception in His saying ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ is connected (istithna' muttasil, exception of the same category). The excepted ones are Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil. It was said: Ridwan, the bearers of the Throne, and the keepers of Paradise and Hell.

﴿Then it will be blown again﴾. ukhra may be in the place of the nominative as a deputy of the subject (naib al-fa'il, the grammatical substitute for the agent), and it is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, meaning: a blast another (nafkhatan ukhra). It may also be in the place of the accusative, and the substitute for the agent in it is:

﴿Then behold, they are standing, looking﴾. Meaning: all the creatures are standing on their feet, looking at what is said to them, or waiting for that.

The majority recited "qiyam" with the nominative, taking it as the predicate, and "yanzuruna" is in the place of the accusative as a circumstantial clause. Zayd ibn 'Ali recited it with the accusative, as a circumstantial element, and the predicate is "yanzuruna." The element that governs the circumstantial is what governs the sudden particle "idha."

al-Kisa'i said: like when you say: "I went out, and behold, Zayd was sitting."

﴿And the earth shone with the light of its Lord﴾. al-Ishraq is illumination. It is said: "the sun shone" when it lit up, and "sharaqat" when it rose. The meaning of "with the light of its Lord" is: with the justice of its Lord, as al-Hasan and others said.

al-Dahhak said: with the judgement of its Lord. The meaning is that the earth lights up and becomes radiant by the justice that Allah established among its people and the truth He decreed concerning them. So justice is light, and injustice is darkness.

It was said: Allah will create a light on the Day of Resurrection, which He will clothe upon the surface of the earth, and it will shine with it, other than the light of the sun and the moon. There is no barrier to taking it in its literal meaning, for Allah, may He be glorified, is the light of the heavens and the earth.

The majority recited "ashraqat" with the active voice. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-Jawza' and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr recited it in the passive voice.

﴿And the Book will be placed﴾. It was said: it is the Preserved Tablet. Qatadah said: meaning the books and scrolls in which are the deeds of the children of Adam, so one takes his book in his right hand and another takes his in his left. Muqatil said likewise. It was said: it is from the placing by the reckoner of the book of reckoning before him, meaning: the Book was placed for the reckoning.

Meaning: they will be brought to the place of standing, and they will be asked about what their nations answered them with, and the witnesses who will testify against the nations from the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), as in His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation, that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. It was said: they are the guardian angels (hafaza), as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾ [Qaf: 21].

﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning: judgement will be passed between the servants with justice and truth, while they are not wronged, meaning they will not have any of their reward diminished, nor will anything be added to the punishment they deserve.

Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Akhfash said: zumaran means companies scattered one after another, and from it is the saying of the poet:

And you see the people at its gates, in groups, one group after another, coming to it.
